Subject: Proposed early renewal accelerator + bridge for 2027 renewal

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Based on your usage trends and the growth signal you shared, I pulled together a short, pragmatic proposal to make the 2027 renewal straightforward while protecting against the end-of-year true-up swing you signaled. I attached a draft (SummitEdge_Renewal_Draft_v3.pdf).

High-level summary:
- Early renewal accelerator: 12-month renewal with a 10% list-rate discount in exchange for a 30% committed uplift vs current baseline (phased across Q1–Q2 to match your ramp).
- True-up smoothing: We propose a lagged true-up where overages in a given quarter are reconciled in the following quarter at a capped rate (see clause 4.2). This reduces short-term invoice volatility for you.
- Bridge credit: Because you are timing a capacity uptake mid-year, we offer a one-time bridge credit ($35k) applied to the first invoice post-signature to offset migration costs.
- SLA credit: If we miss the 99.9% latency SLO for API calls during the first 90 days after migration, we will provide a service credit equal to 5% of that quarter's invoice.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Quick alignment call this week (30 min) to confirm ramp cadence and any legal redlines.
2) If alignment OK, we finalize an addendum and DocuSign packet for signatures.

Would you be available Wed or Thu afternoon PT?

Best,
Diego Fernandez

Short answers:
- Lagged true-up math (summary): Overages are measured by actual consumption vs committed usage for each calendar quarter. Instead of billing immediate overages at quarter end, we bill them in the following quarter at the agreed capped rate. Practically: Q1 overage => invoiced in Q2. This allows you to plan for the additional spend in the next billing period and smooths cash flow. In the attached section 4.2 we show an example calculation for a 20% overage on a $200k quarter.
- Credit visibility: The bridge credit will be a line-item credit on the first invoice after signature. We can include a purchase-order reference or internal account memo so procurement sees it clearly.
